Subject: Post-demo shortlist + veto triggers & regression guardrails

Hi Daniel / Sofia —

Great to meet you this morning — appreciate the clear framing on the summarization and redaction constraints. Quick recap and our recommended engine shortlist based on the demo session and the evaluation criteria you gave (fidelity on legal/PII redaction, sub-second median latency for short summaries, and cost sensitivity at scale).

Recommended shortlist (priority order):
- rwd-optimized-7b (best quality/latency balance for multi-doc summarization)
- rwd-quant-4b (cost-first; good latency, slight drop on adversarial redaction cases)
- open-compat-6b (fallback option where a less-conservative safety profile is acceptable)

Rationale (concise):
- rwd-optimized-7b: most consistent on the 8 example prompts you provided in the call — p95 latency ~420ms on our 4-core dedicated config, lowest perceptible hallucination on legal clauses. Unit cost estimate: medium (approx $0.012 / 1k tokens served) with caching enabled.
- rwd-quant-4b: ~30–40% lower token cost, p95 latency ~310ms; we saw occasional redaction misses on adversarially-worded examples (we recommended augmenting prompt guardrails).
- open-compat-6b: good baseline, easiest to port on-prem; quality sits between the two Redwood options.

Veto triggers / regression guardrails (what we'd commit to watch during pilot):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end > 500ms on your typical 300–600 token jobs (unacceptable)
- Redaction regression: any drop >5 percentage points in redaction recall on the core prompt set
- Quality drift: manual QA failure rate >7% on the 50-case weekly random sample
- Cost overshoot: realized token spend >25% above forecast in first billing month without prior approval

Attachments included: prompt pack we used in the demo (brightbridge_prompt_pack_v1.txt), our latency baseline CSV (latency_benchmarks_4cores.csv), and the demo recording (redwood_demo_recording.mp4). Links to the same artifacts are below.

Next steps / asks from you:
1) Confirm which engines you want us to evaluate in a short A/B pilot (pick 2 preferred, 1 fallback).
2) Tell us which three production prompts you want to use as the priority regression set (we used three during the demo; attach if different).
3) If procurement wants a commercial/po path now, share the procurement contact and preferred timeline — we can provide a provisional cost worksheet.

If helpful, we can run a two-week pilot against the three-priority prompts with daily regression alerts and a weekly summary call. Proposed pilot kickoff: next Monday (2028-07-24).

Thanks again — I'll coordinate the evaluation package once you confirm the engines.

Best,
Jonas Weber

- On-prem: we have an internal requirement that some workloads must be runnable in our VPC — how different is the performance profile for rwd-optimized-7b if we run in BrightBridge's us-west cluster (we have 8xA10g-equivalent GPUs)?

Also — I could see our security team asking for tighter redaction guarantees. The veto triggers make sense; can you add an example of what remediation looks like if we see a redaction miss during pilot? (E.g., prompt tuning, fine-tune, policy layer).

Finally, agree on a pilot but can we shift kickoff to Wednesday (2028-07-26) to give the security team time to review the prompt pack?

Cheers,
DP

Thanks Daniel — answers inline and attachments below.

- Cost table: attached (latency_benchmarks_4cores.csv includes a pricing tab). Short answer (estimates for 1M calls/month at ~420 tokens/call):
  • rwd-optimized-7b — High: $16,800 / month, Likely: $12,600 / month, Low: $10,400 / month
  • rwd-quant-4b — High: $10,400 / month, Likely: $7,000 / month, Low: $5,600 / month

- On-prem performance: With your 8xA10g-equivalent VPC, we expect p95 reduction ~10–15% vs our shared hosted baseline. We can include that as an explicit expectation in the SOW and instrument additional tracing to verify.

- Remediation for redaction misses (example runbook):
  1) Flag & rollback: automatic alert to CS + security on any redaction miss in the pilot sample — we route affected calls to rwd-optimized-7b and enable post-process redact filter (regex/NER).
  2) Prompt-hardening iteration: we add targeted negative examples to the prompt pack and re-run the regression suite (typically closes ~60–80% of misses).
  3) If required, execute a small fine-tune/rlhf pass restricted to anonymized examples (only if the customer approves data usage) — rare, only for systematic failure modes.

We're fine to shift pilot kickoff to Wednesday 2028-07-26 to allow security review — please confirm and we'll lock resources (Marissa will drop the SOW text into HubSpot).

Next steps for us (I'll do these once you confirm engines & kickoff date):
- Upload cost table & pilot SOW to the HubSpot deal (link below).
- Provision two evaluation endpoints (rwd-optimized-7b, rwd-quant-4b) with daily regression runs and alerting.
- Run the initial 50-case regression suite and share results within 72 hours of kickoff.
